Hey folks! I'm back with my second round of making a 1 gal batch of semi-sweet mead. I learned a lot from my first attempt, after reading more and talking to more experienced brewers, I realized I went about things incorrectly. I will try to describe my process as best as possible and show a few pictures at the end!

Step 1) Sanitize!

I started by mixing 1 gallon of distilled water with 2oz of Sodium Metabisulfite, a common sanitizer you can pick up at any store. I was able to get 2oz for about $1.50. I washed and sanitized all my equipment and surfaces before starting. From everything I've read, this step is extremely important so you won't have lots of rogue bacteria in your must, which can ruin it.

Step 2) Create the must

Next I added about 1/2 gallon of distilled water to my 1 gallon carboy. Pretty simple, just pour it in at this point. Then I added 3lbs of honey. 2lbs gives you a dry mead, 3.8lbs gives you a sweet mead, so I went in the middle to get a semi-sweet mead. After the honey was added, I mixed two cups of spring water in a separate mixing bowl along with 1 teaspoon of yeast energizer and 1 teaspoon of yeast nutrient. I mixed it up until there no were no chunks left in it, then poured it into the carboy with the honey / water mix.

After all that was added, I put a stopper into the carboy, and shook vigorously for about 5 minutes, stopping half way through and uncapping it to let any gases release.

Step 3) The Yeast!

On a stove, I heated two cups of distilled water to about 105-107 degree Fahrenheit. Be very careful not to make your water too hot because it can insta-kill the yeast. Once heating, remove the water from the stove and put it in your mixing bowl. I added my yeast but did not stir it. I let it sit for about 15 minutes, then gave it a gentle stir and added it into the carboy with the rest of the must.

Step 4) Shake shake shake!

I filled my carboy up the rest of the way with distilled water, leaving a small amount of room at the top for air. I put a stopper in it and I shook it vigorously for about 10-15 mintes (this part is a freakin' workout). Make sure to shake it very well because this will aerate the must, which is important for the fermentation process.

Step 5) Finishing Touches

After that was done, I put my stopper with a hole in the carboy, added water to my airlock, and placed the airlock in the stopper. You want to keep this in a cool dark place, as light (especially UV light) can skunk your brew and kill the yeast.

That's pretty much it! Pretty straightforward, nothing fancy, but I will make another post when I rack the must and keep everyone updated on how it turns out!
